full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury, J: Respondents Nos. 1-5 have been implicated in G.R. Case No. 104 of 1997 of the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Munshiganj upon suspicion of having committed murder of Rafiqul Islam, the uncle of respondent Nos. 1-4. 

 2. Rafiqul Islam was found dead in his house and was duly buried but his daughter Afroza Monjur initiated the case on allegation that there was enmity between her father and the accused-persons on account of litigation over properties and the accused-persons had poisoned her father to death. The dead body was exhumed and postmortem examined by the doctor who was not certain about cause of death. 

 3. The respondents approached the Vacation Bench of the High Court Division with an application marked as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2114 of 1998 on 6 April 1998 for anticipatory bail on the ground that the death of the deceased was caused by natural illness and over does of medicine and the respondents were implicated out of enmity. Furthermore the case was started after long 7 months of the occurrence and it was a concocted one. The said Bench granted them anticipatory bail till re-opening; 

 6. We have gone through the grounds and facts of the case. We are of the view that the observations are not inappropriate. Furthermore, no prayer for leave has been made.
